2.name: Asha calls Mrs. Adelman
2.description: Asha phones Mrs. Adelman, who answers as if expecting exactly this call.
evidence: Asha then called Mrs. Adelman, two doors down on Pemberton Street, who answered on the third ring in a voice that suggested she had been hoping someone would call her about exactly this.

2.name: Mrs. Adelman recalls signing the document
2.description: Mrs. Adelman says she remembers the signing clearly and explains that Helena invited her over with sherry and a brief request.
evidence: "I remember it perfectly," Mrs. Adelman said.

"It was a Tuesday because I had bridge that night and I almost said no, but Helena said it would only take twenty minutes and she would give me a glass of sherry, which she did, and it was the good sherry, not the kitchen sherry."

2.name: Mrs. Adelman signs under Helena's signature
2.description: Mrs. Adelman confirms she signed the document beneath Helena's signature while a lawyer supervised the reading.
evidence: "I signed under her signature. The lawyer was a small man with very neat handwriting. He had me read the page first. He said it was important that I had read it."

2.name: Mrs. Adelman recounts will changes
2.description: Mrs. Adelman remembers the document redirecting property to Lucia Serrano and increasing Daniel's cash bequest as compensation.
evidence: "It said—" Mrs. Adelman paused. "It said that notwithstanding the prior will, the property at—the address, you know—was to go to her daughter Lucia Serrano. There was a sentence about Daniel. It said the cash bequest to him was being increased to compensate."

2.name: Mrs. Adelman judges Helena deliberate
2.description: Mrs. Adelman reflects that Helena had carefully considered the changes and was not impulsive.
evidence: "I remember thinking that was a lot of money. I remember thinking Helena had thought about it carefully. She was not a woman who did things in a hurry."

2.name: Asha records the testimony
2.description: Asha writes down Mrs. Adelman's account word for word with careful precision.
evidence: Asha wrote it down word for word. Her pen moved very evenly.

2.name: Asha confirms the date
2.description: Asha presses Mrs. Adelman to verify the date of the signing, and Mrs. Adelman gives a specific September 12 date.
evidence: "Mrs. Adelman, I have to ask. Are you sure of the date."
"September the twelfth. I marked it because she gave me sherry on a weekday. I have a calendar where I note such things."

2.name: Mrs. Adelman says lawyer took the file
2.description: Mrs. Adelman says the lawyer placed the signed document in a blue folder and likely took it away.
evidence: "And the lawyer took the document with him."
"He put it in a file. A blue folder. I assume he took it. I didn't watch him le"

2.name: Mrs. Adelman confirms lawyer took document
2.description: Mrs. Adelman explains that the lawyer took the document, filed it in a blue folder, and she did not watch him leave.
evidence: "And the lawyer took the document with him."
"He put it in a file. A blue folder. I assume he took it. I didn't watch him leave."

2.name: Mrs. Adelman expresses loyalty to Helena
2.description: Mrs. Adelman thanks Asha and says Helena was good to her, hoping the matter will come out right.
evidence: "Thank you."
"Helena was good to me," Mrs. Adelman said. "I would like this to come out right."

2.name: Asha requests physical archive search
2.description: Asha calls the successor firm again and asks them to check the physical archive for a blue folder with Helena Serrano's name and a September twelfth date.
evidence: Asha set down the phone and sat for a long moment with her hand still on it.

Then she called the successor firm again and asked, in the politest possible voice, whether someone could check the physical archive, not just the digital one, for a blue folder bearing Helena Serrano's name and a date of September twelfth.

2.name: Receptionist promises callback
2.description: The receptionist tells Asha she will have to call back later after checking the archive request.
evidence: "I'll have to call you back," the receptionist said.

2.name: Lucia contacts Asha secretly
2.description: Lucia calls Asha using Rosa's help to get her direct line and says she needs to speak without Daniel present.
evidence: That afternoon Lucia called her.
"Rosa gave it to me," Lucia said. "I hope that's all right. I needed to talk to you without Daniel in the house."

2.name: Lucia says Daniel is meeting agent secretly
2.description: Lucia tells Asha that Daniel has gone to meet with an agent, despite claiming he is not meeting with one.
evidence: "He's gone to meet with the agent. The one he says he's not meeting with."

2.name: Lucia reveals hidden letter
2.description: Lucia tells Asha she found a handwritten letter in the sewing room that was addressed to her and appears to be from her mother.
evidence: "There's a letter," Lucia said. "I found it in the sewing room three days ago, before you came. It was in the drawer of the side table where Mom kept her thimbles. It's in her handwriting. It is addressed to me."

2.name: Lucia reports changed will
2.description: Lucia begins reading the letter, which says her mother changed her will and wanted Lucia to know directly in case the paperwork was lost.
evidence: "It says—" She stopped.
"It says she has changed her will. It says she wanted me to know directly, in case anything happened to the paperwork."

2.name: Lucia begins revealing letter's trust statement
2.description: Lucia starts to say that the letter states her mother trusts someone, but the message cuts off before the full statement is revealed.
evidence: "It says she trusts m"

2.name: Lucia reveals changed will letter
2.description: Lucia tells Asha that Rosa has written a letter saying she changed her will and wanted Lucia to know directly.
evidence: "It says she has changed her will. It says she wanted me to know directly, in case anything happened to the paperwork."

2.name: Lucia explains Rosa's wishes
2.description: Lucia says Rosa trusted her to be kind to Daniel, expected him to be angry, and believed the house should be lived in rather than sold.
evidence: "It says she trusts me to be kind to Daniel about it. She says she knows he will be angry. She says the house should be lived in, and she does not believe Daniel will live in it."

2.name: Lucia admits she hid the letter
2.description: Lucia confesses that she has not shown the letter to anyone else.
evidence: "I haven't shown it to anyone."

2.name: Lucia explains delayed disclosure
2.description: Lucia says she is telling Asha now because she wants to handle the situation properly and avoid ambushing Daniel or being blamed for breaking the family.
evidence: "Because if Daniel sells the house and the codicil never turns up, the letter is just a sentimental object. I want to do this right. I don't want to ambush him. I don't want—"
"I don't want to be the one who broke this family. I want her to be the one who decided. Does that make sense."

2.name: Asha asserts involvement
2.description: Asha tells Lucia that the matter is no longer entirely Lucia's decision and asks to see the letter today.
evidence: "It makes sense," Asha said. "It is also not entirely your decision anymore."
"I need to see the letter."
"Today."

2.name: Lucia arranges nighttime meeting
2.description: Lucia tells Asha to come that night after eight because Daniel will be gone.
evidence: "Come tonight. After eight. He'll be gone."

2.name: Asha reflects on family entanglement
2.description: After the call, Asha recognizes she is being drawn into the Serrano family's conflict and reminds herself to keep compassion separate from neutrality.
evidence: Asha closed her eyes for a moment after she hung up.
She was aware, with the clarity that her work required, that she was being drawn into the gravity of this family.
"Compassion was not neutrality, and the rule was the only thing that kept the two from collapsing into each other."

2.name: Asha returns to Serrano house
2.description: Asha goes back to the Serrano house later that evening to meet Lucia.
evidence: She went back to the Serrano house at half past eight.

2.name: reaffirm compassion rule
2.description: Asha reflects on her rule that compassion must not be confused with neutrality, treating it as a necessary boundary.
evidence: She had a rule about that. Compassion was not neutrality, and the rule was the only thing that kept the two from collapsing into each other.

2.name: return to Serrano house
2.description: Asha goes back to the Serrano house in the evening as the rain returns.
evidence: She went back to the Serrano house at half past eight.
The rain had returned, finer now, more like mist.

2.name: Rosa admits Asha
2.description: Rosa lets Asha into the house even though her presence at that hour is technically improper.
evidence: Rosa let her in.
Rosa was not supposed to be there at that hour, technically, but Rosa was there, and Asha did not comment on it.

2.name: find Lucia's letter
2.description: Asha finds a letter addressed to Lucia waiting in the sewing room.
evidence: Lucia was in the sewing room at the back of the house, a small bright room with a treadle machine in the corner and a window that looked out on the garden where the wisteria was sleeping.
The letter was on the worktable, in an envelope with Lucia's name written on the front in blue ink.

2.name: read the letter
2.description: Asha reads the letter standing in the sewing room and recognizes the handwriting as the same one she had been studying all afternoon.
evidence: Asha read it standing up.
The signature at the bottom was the same firm round hand she had been looking at all afternoon.

2.name: reveal house transfer
2.description: The letter reveals that the house has been formally given to Lucia after years of delay.
evidence: I have done something I should have done five years ago.
Mr. Pinsky came today and we have set it down properly. The house is yours.

2.name: justify inheritance decision
2.description: The letter explains that Lucia receives the house because she stayed there when the writer was afraid, and the house remembers that.
evidence: Not because Daniel does not deserve a house.
Because you have been the one who slept under this roof when I was afraid, and a house remembers that.

2.name: compensate Daniel
2.description: The writer says she has given Daniel money to balance the gift of the house.
evidence: I have given him money to make it even.

2.name: warn Lucia about Daniel
2.description: The letter warns Lucia that Daniel will be hurt and asks her to be patient with him.
evidence: He will be hurt and you will have to be patient with him.
You are better at patience than he is.

2.name: praise Lucia's patience
2.description: The letter closes this section by affirming Lucia's patience and character as something Daniel has not fully recognized.
evidence: You have always been better than he knows.

2.name: letter confirms codicil details
2.description: The letter is read as containing specific references to the codicil and the filing location without contradicting Mrs. Adelman's account.
evidence: It mentioned the codicil by name. It said where the original was meant to be filed. It did not say anything that contradicted what Mrs. Adelman had told her on the phone.

2.name: Asha reviews the letter
2.description: Asha folds the letter back into its envelope and pauses with it in her hands, considering its significance.
evidence: Asha folded the letter back into its envelope and held it in both hands for a moment.

2.name: Asha distinguishes evidence from codicil
2.description: Asha explains to Lucia that the letter shows intent and corroborates witnesses, but is not itself a valid codicil.
evidence: "Lucia," she said. "This is evidence of intent. It is not, by itself, a codicil. A holographic instrument in Pennsylvania has to meet certain requirements, and this letter is not trying to be a will. It does corroborate Mrs. Adelman and Rosa. It corroborates them strongly."

2.name: Lucia confirms need for codicil
2.description: Lucia acknowledges that the legal team still needs the actual codicil document.
evidence: "So we still need the codicil itself."

2.name: Asha explains fallback legal strategy
2.description: Asha says the successor firm is searching for the original and outlines a harder, slower argument if it cannot be found.
evidence: "Ideally. The successor firm is searching. If the original cannot be found, there are arguments I can make based on the witness testimony and this letter, but they are harder, and they will be uglier, and they will take longer, and the longer they take the more the estate bleeds. I would like to find the document."

2.name: Lucia asks about failure case
2.description: Lucia presses Asha on what happens if the codicil cannot be found.
evidence: "And if you cannot."

2.name: Asha leaves decision to Lucia
2.description: Asha tells Lucia that choosing the harder legal argument will be Lucia's decision, though Asha will advise her.
evidence: "Then we will have a conversation about whether you want to make the harder argument. That will be your call. I will tell you what I think. But I will not make it for you."

2.name: Lucia appears exhausted
2.description: Lucia silently accepts the explanation and looks very tired while Rosa watches from the doorway.
evidence: Lucia nodded. She looked very tired. Rosa, in the doorway, was watching them both with an expression Asha could not quite read.

2.name: Asha begins another warning
2.description: Asha introduces one more important matter and starts to tell Lucia something she needs to know.
evidence: "There is one more thing," Asha said. "You need to tell

2.name: Lucia agrees to tell her brother
2.description: Asha tells Lucia she must inform her brother about the letter soon, and Lucia accepts that she should hear it from her.
evidence: "There is one more thing," Asha said. "You need to tell your brother about this letter. Not tonight. But soon. Before I have to. I would rather he hear it from you."
"He'll think I planted it."
"He will think a lot of things. None of them will be true and none of them will matter in court. But they will matter at this table for the rest of your life."
"Will you be there when I tell him."
"Yes," Asha said. "If you want me to be."
"I want you to be."

2.name: They set Friday for the disclosure
2.description: Asha and Lucia agree to wait until Friday to tell Lucia's brother about the letter.
evidence: They agreed on Friday.

2.name: Asha gains three days to find codicil
2.description: Asha realizes she has three more days to locate the codicil, which she believes will determine whether the case ends cleanly.
evidence: That gave Asha three more days to find the codicil itself, which was, she had begun to suspect, going to be the difference between this story ending cleanly and ending the way most of her cases did, which was with everyone alive but no one quite speaking.

2.name: Successor firm returns archive findings
2.description: The successor firm calls Asha back and a young apologetic paralegal named Marcus reports what he found in the physical archive.
evidence: The next morning the successor firm called back.
A paralegal named Marcus, who sounded young and who sounded apologetic.

2.name: Marcus finds Serrano file and notes
2.description: Marcus says the archive contains a Serrano file with the executed will, correspondence, and Pinsky's handwritten notes from a September meeting.
evidence: He had gone through the physical archive.
There was a Serrano file.

It contained the executed will from eleven years ago, two pieces of correspondence, and a folder marked September, which contained Mr. Pinsky's handwritten notes from a client meeting on September twelfth

2.name: Notes mention codicil executed
2.description: The handwritten notes include an entry stating that a codicil was executed with two witnesses and returned to the client.
evidence: including the phrase "codicil executed, two witnesses, original to client per instruction."

2.name: Asha questions retention of original
2.description: Asha repeats the phrase 'per instruction' and begins pressing Marcus about whether Pinsky kept the original document.
evidence: "Per instruction," Asha repeated.
"That's what the note says."
"So Pinsky did not retain the or

2.name: Asha returns to Pemberton Street
2.description: Asha drives back to Pemberton Street that afternoon to continue the investigation.
evidence: She drove back to Pemberton Street that afternoon.

2.name: Daniel has effectively moved in
2.description: Asha realizes Daniel is now staying at the house regularly, with his belongings and work setup taking over the space.
evidence: Daniel was there. Daniel was always there now, she realized. He had moved in, or as good as.
There was a duffel bag at the foot of the stairs and a laptop open on the dining table and the smell of takeout coffee in cups that were not the family's cups.

2.name: Daniel confronts Asha for not calling
2.description: Daniel sharply objects that Asha did not call before coming over.
evidence: He looked up sharply when she came in.
"You didn't call."

2.name: Asha apologizes and announces an update
2.description: Asha apologizes for not calling and says she has an update for Daniel and Lucia.
evidence: "I should have. I'm sorry. I have an update."

2.name: Lucia joins the conversation
2.description: Lucia comes downstairs after hearing the voices, while Rosa remains absent.
evidence: Lucia came down the stairs behind her, hearing the voices.
Rosa, Asha noted, did not appear.

2.name: Family shifts meeting to the parlor
2.description: They move the discussion to the parlor because Daniel has taken over the dining table as his office, and Asha notices Helena's abandoned belongings there.
evidence: They sat in the parlor this time, because the dining table was Daniel's office now.
The parlor was where Helena had spent her evenings.

There was an armchair near the window with a quilt thrown over the back and a side table with a pair of reading glasses still on it and a paperback face down, splayed open at a page Helena had not finished.
Asha tried not to look at the chair.

2.name: Asha reports the codicil was executed
2.description: Asha tells Daniel and Lucia that the codicil was signed, citing Pinsky's file and the September twelfth meeting with witnesses.
evidence: "The codicil was executed," she said.
"I have notes from Pinsky's file confirming the meeting on September twelfth, the witnesses, and the fact that a codicil was signed."

2.name: Asha reveals Pinsky gave original to mother
2.description: Asha explains that Pinsky gave the original codicil to their mother and kept no copy in his file.
evidence: "Pinsky gave the original to your mother. He did not retain a copy in his file."

2.name: Daniel accuses Pinsky of malpractice
2.description: Daniel reacts to the revelation by calling the transfer of the original malpractice.
evidence: Daniel did not move. "He gave her the original."
"That's malpractice."

2.name: Asha qualifies the legal significance
2.description: Asha pushes back, saying the act was unusual but not necessarily malpractice because it was done at the mother's request.
evidence: "It is unusual. It is not, by itself, malpractice. It was at her request."

2.name: reveal original was given away
2.description: Daniel learns that the original document was given to her rather than kept in the file.
evidence: "He gave her the original."
"Yes."

2.name: Daniel accuses malpractice
2.description: Daniel reacts strongly, calling the decision to give away the original malpractice.
evidence: "That's malpractice."

2.name: Asha defends unusual request
2.description: Asha explains that the act was unusual but not necessarily malpractice because it was done at her request.
evidence: "It is unusual. It is not, by itself, malpractice. It was at her request."

2.name: locate original in house
2.description: Asha suggests the original may still be in the house and that they need to search for it.
evidence: "So the original is in this house."
"Possibly. Or it was. We need to look."

2.name: Daniel reports exhaustive search
2.description: Daniel says he has already searched every drawer in the house and found no codicil.
evidence: "We have looked," Daniel said.
"I have been through every drawer in this house. There is no codicil."

2.name: Asha absorbs Daniel's claim
2.description: Asha lets Daniel's statement hang in the silence while Lucia watches her brother.
evidence: Asha let that sit in the air.
Lucia was watching her brother.
